rule: Two-sided ideal criterion for the kernel of a ring homomorphism

conditions.condition: ker(phi) is nonempty and closed under subtraction, hence an additive subgroup of R.
conditions.justification: A ring homomorphism sends 0_R to 0_S, while the prior node supplies subtraction closure; the nonempty subtraction test gives an additive subgroup.

conditions.condition: For every r in R and x in ker(phi), both rx and xr are in ker(phi).
conditions.justification: Multiplicativity and phi(x)=0 give phi(rx)=phi(r)phi(x)=0 and phi(xr)=phi(x)phi(r)=0.

circularity.justification: The ideal conditions are verified directly from homomorphism properties and the established additive closure, not from the theorem target.

conclusion.statement: Because phi(0_R) = 0_S, the kernel is nonempty; together with closure under subtraction, this makes ker(phi) an additive subgroup of R. If r is in R and x is in ker(phi), then phi(rx) = phi(r)phi(x) = 0 and phi(xr) = phi(x)phi(r) = 0, so rx and xr are in ker(phi). Therefore ker(phi) is a two-sided ideal of R.
conclusion.justification: The nonempty additive subgroup condition together with absorption under multiplication on both sides is exactly the two-sided ideal criterion.

reason: The repaired node supplies the previously missing two-sided absorption proof and correctly completes the ideal argument.
